_meta.indication: Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study CBAF312A2304 (A2304), the single pivotal Phase 3 trial
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-national, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven study; patients randomized 2:1 to siponimod (titrated to 2 mg oral daily) or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with protocol-defined secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS), with baseline EDSS of 3.0 to 6.5
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was time to 3-month confirmed disability progression (CDP) as measured by the EDSS
pivotal_trials.result: 3-month CDP occurred in 288/1096 (26.3%) siponimod vs 173/545 (31.7%) placebo; 21.2% relative risk reduction, 5.4% absolute risk reduction, hazard ratio 0.79 (95% CI 0.65, 0.95), p=0.0134

nct_ctgov.title: Exploring the Efficacy and Safety of Siponimod in Patients With Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (EXPAND)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >10%) are headache (15% vs 14% placebo), hypertension (13% vs 9%), and transaminase increases (11% vs 3%); other reactions include falls (11% vs 10%), peripheral edema (8% vs 4%), and bradycardia (6% vs 3%). Serious risks include bradyarrhythmia and atrioventricular conduction delays, infections, macular edema, and a decline in pulmonary function (FEV1).
target_moa: Siponimod is a sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds selectively to the S1P1 and S1P5 receptors; it promotes internalization and degradation of S1P1 receptors, acting as a functional antagonist that reduces recirculation of T-cells into the CNS to limit central inflammation
companion_dx_detail: CYP2C9 genotype testing is required prior to treatment to guide dosing and identify contraindicated CYP2C9*3/*3 patients, but no FDA-cleared or -approved test for CYP2C9 variants to direct siponimod use is currently available

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an Advisory Committee because the drug is not first in its class and its safety profile is similar to that of other drugs

description.text: Labeling update to add lesser identified CYP2C9 polymorphisms and amend vaccine recommendations; no new indication or population added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for an update to the prescribing information (PI) to include lesser identified CYP2C9 polymorphisms in Use in Specific Populations (8.6) and Clinical Pharmacology (12.5) sections, and to amend the current vaccine recommendations to prescribers in the Warnings and Precautions (5.1) and Drug Interactions (7.4) sections of the PI.

basis.text: A Fast Track application for the indication of the treatment of SPMS was granted in September 2012

citations.quote: In April 2012, the applicant submitted the protocol for Study A2304 with a request for a SPA. SPA agreement was reached in August 2012. A Fast Track application for the indication of the treatment of SPMS was granted in September 2012,

summary.text: Siponimod (a new molecular entity) received Fast Track designation for the SPMS indication in September 2012 and was approved on the first review cycle based on the single pivotal Phase 3 trial A2304; the application was not referred to an advisory committee. This was a standard (non-accelerated) approval with no breakthrough, orphan, or priority review designations noted.

requirement.text: 3591-3: A prospective, parallel cohort study in patients with relapsing forms of MS to assess the potentially serious risk of pulmonary toxicity, comparing patients newly prescribed siponimod with patients receiving another MS drug

citations.quote: 3591-3 A prospective, parallel cohort study in patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis to assess the potentially serious risk of pulmonary toxicity. The two cohorts should consist of patients newly prescribed siponimod and patients receiving another drug used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.

requirement.text: 3591-4: A prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with MS exposed to siponimod during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations

citations.quote: 3591-4 Conduct prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with multiple sclerosis exposed to siponimod during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations: one consisting of women with multiple sclerosis who have not been exposed to siponimod before or during pregnancy, and the other consisting of women without multiple sclerosis.

requirement.text: 3591-5: A pregnancy outcomes study using a different design (e.g., retrospective cohort or case control) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to siponimod during pregnancy versus an unexposed control population

citations.quote: 3591-5 Conduct a pregnancy outcomes study using a different study design than provided for in PMR 3591-4 (for example, a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to siponimod during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3591-6: Establish an in-vitro diagnostic device to guide the use of siponimod, detecting at a minimum the *2 and *3 alleles in CYP2C9 and identifying patients homozygous for the CYP2C9*3/*3 genotype

citations.quote: 3591-6 Establish an in-vitro diagnostic device to guide the use of siponimod in patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis. The device should detect, at a minimum, the presence of the *2 and *3 alleles in cytochrome P450 2C9 (CYP2C9). The device should detect patients homozygous for the CYP2C9 *3/*3 genotype with statistical confidence.
